title: My game absolutely CRASHED Steam wishlists!
author: GiftedMamba
selftext:
After weeks of development and marketing, my upcoming co-op game Gravity Express has finally reached an incredible milestone.

**9 wishlists.**

Yes, nine. Single digits. Steam's servers somehow survived. :D

The funny thing is, everyone who's actually played the game seems to enjoy it. But convincing people to give it a try? That's apparently the real final boss.

Anyway, here's some gameplay. At least the crashes in the game are more spectacular than my marketing efforts!

  
**How was it developed?**

I actually have a pretty complicated AI-driven pipeline for developing my current games, but this one started with a single question in mind:

**What can current LLMs do with absolutely NO guidance at all? No skills, no Agent/Claude.md, nothing. Just an obsidian vault to allow Opus to make notes and my feedback from playtests.**

So everything you see here, except for the game design (100% human-made! :D), was created by Opus 5.5. Code, models, textures, animations, UI - everything.

I initially started developing the game in Three.js. I know it's quite popular for agentic development nowadays, but by day three, I had already migrated to Unity. Three.js was simply missing too many features that I had absolutely no desire to recreate, even with vibe coding.

Opus ported the Three.js version to Unity in about **4 hours**.

The biggest problem was physics. Unity's built-in physics felt completely different from Rapier, which I had been using in the Three.js version.

The solution? Well, **Opus 5.5 ported Rapier to Unity in 2 hours.** :D

I also ran a small experiment: same stage of development, same feature, two different engines.

* **Three.js:** 38 minutes
* **Unity:** 43 minutes

It turned out that once the project reached a certain level of complexity, there was almost no meaningful difference in development speed. And the Unity version looked better right out of the box.

So I decided to stick with Unity.

Now, speaking as a professional developer with over 10 years of experience in games, simulations, and VR, who has also built several games entirely by hand:

**LLMs are pure magic. They're the best thing that has ever happened to game development as a creative process.** I'd even argue that the arrival of free-to-use game engines wasn't nearly as dramatic a change.

Before LLMs, game development often felt like this:

*95% of my time was spent figuring out how to implement something or Googling solutions, and only 5% was spent actually creating the game I had in mind.*

Now it feels like the opposite.

And it's pure joy.

Have fun building! :D

**P.S.** If you'd like to play a fun, charming co-op game with your partner, family, or friends, here's the Steam page for Gravity Express:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5380470/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5380470/)
